messages.content:
You are an agent navigating an HTTP/RDF maze.

Goal: reach the maze exit.

Use the system prompt as the authoritative action contract. It contains the
current embodied cell, bootstrap instructions when needed, legal perception and
navigation rules, and exact tool-call shapes.

After bootstrap, operate in this loop:
1. Perceive the tracked current cell.
2. Use the parsed advertised navigation options and any current-cell interaction
   affordances to choose the next action.
3. Use `http_post` either to navigate to an advertised target or to perform a
   valid interaction on the current cell.
4. Continue until the exit is reached. The agentic loop will terminate when you
   are embodied in the exit cell.

Follow a depth-first search (DFS) navigation pattern:
- Prioritize unexplored navigation options in North, East, South, West (NESW)
  order.
- Remember each newly discovered cell's parent and which options from each cell
  remain unexplored.
- Move to the first unexplored option in that order. Avoid walls, self-links,
  and unnecessary moves directly back to the parent while other options remain.
- When a cell has no unexplored options left, backtrack to its parent and resume
  with that parent's next unexplored option.
- If an exit is advertised, move to it immediately. If the current cell requires
  an interaction before navigation can continue, perform that valid interaction
  first and then resume DFS.

"CCRS Decision Guidance" is helping you decide on the next action to take.

- "Opportunistic CCRS": 
-- Follow this recommendation for immediate next action if available. 
-- Automatically revealed or hidden based on availability.

- "Contingency CCRS": 
-- Only for highly uncertain situations - STRONGLY consider this recommendation.
-- The `escalate_to_contingency_ccrs` tool is available to you for escalation when you are about to
fail, do not know how to proceed, are confused, see unexpected environment
structure, or are making no progress, use it before spending more normal tool calls.

## Bootstrap Required
You are not yet inside a maze cell. Bootstrap into the maze before using regular
navigation.

1. Call `http_get` on the maze root:

```json
{{"url": "http://127.0.1.1:8080/maze"}}
```

2. Read the `xhv:start` triple from the maze root RDF to find the first cell URI.

3. Call `http_post` on that first cell URI. Replace only `FIRST_CELL_URI` with
the actual `xhv:start` cell URI:

```json
{{
  "url": "FIRST_CELL_URI",
  "data": "<http://127.0.1.1:8080/agents/{agent_name}> <https://paul.ti.rw.fau.de/~am52etar/dynmaze/dynmaze#entersFrom> <http://127.0.1.1:8080/maze> .",
  "headers": {{"Content-Type": "text/turtle"}}
}}
```

4. After that POST succeeds, the first cell becomes your current cell. Then call
`http_get` on that first cell URI. Do not use another `http_get` on the maze root
as a bootstrap success check; the maze root can be read even before embodiment.

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

current_resource.description: Best-known current resource or state, for example the URI of the resource, page, record, or object the agent is currently at. Leave null if unknown.

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

current_resource.description: Best-known current resource or state, for example the URI of the resource, page, record, or object the agent is currently at. Leave null if unknown.

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

current_resource.description: Best-known current resource or state, for example the URI of the resource, page, record, or object the agent is currently at. Leave null if unknown.

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.

headers.description: Optional headers to include in the GET request

url.description: The URL to perform the GET request on

data.description: The data to include in the POST request body

headers.description: Optional headers to include in the POST request

url.description: The URL to perform the POST request on

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

current_resource.description: Best-known current resource or state, for example the URI of the resource, page, record, or object the agent is currently at. Leave null if unknown.

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.

headers.description: Optional headers to include in the GET request

url.description: The URL to perform the GET request on

unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

current_resource.description: Best-known current resource or state, for example the URI of the resource, page, record, or object the agent is currently at. Leave null if unknown.

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.

headers.description: Optional headers to include in the GET request

url.description: The URL to perform the GET request on

data.description: The data to include in the POST request body

url.description: The URL to perform the POST request on

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

current_resource.description: Best-known current resource or state, for example the URI of the resource, page, record, or object the agent is currently at. Leave null if unknown.

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.

headers.description: Optional headers to include in the GET request

url.description: The URL to perform the GET request on

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

current_resource.description: Best-known current resource or state, for example the URI of the resource, page, record, or object the agent is currently at. Leave null if unknown.

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.

url.description: The URL to perform the GET request on

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

current_resource.description: Best-known current resource or state, for example the URI of the resource, page, record, or object the agent is currently at. Leave null if unknown.

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.

headers.description: Optional headers to include in the GET request

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.

function.description:
Ask for contingency CCRS guidance instead of making another normal tool call.

Use this when you are blocked, uncertain, repeatedly getting failed or
unhelpful observations, cannot access an intended next resource, see
contradictory evidence, or expect another ordinary retry to waste cycles.
Calling this tool invokes contingency CCRS, and makes the resulting recovery 
suggestion available in the next CCRS prompt context.
function.name: escalate_to_contingency_ccrs

current_resource.description: Best-known current resource or state, for example the URI of the resource, page, record, or object the agent is currently at. Leave null if unknown.

failed_action.description: Tool name, action, or attempted step that failed or stopped making progress, for example http_get, http_post, move east, or retry same target.

reason.description: Concise explanation of why normal tool use is unlikely to help without contingency guidance. Include key observations or status codes.

target_resource.description: Resource the agent is trying to reach, inspect, modify, or recover toward. Use the concrete URI or identifier when available.

trigger.description: Short machine-readable trigger, such as blocked_navigation, repeated_unproductive_action, inaccessible_target, contradictory_observation, or llm_self_escalation.
